messages:
olivia: Hey team — Acme POC next week. They're evaluating Private deploy and need a clear recommendation: VPC Peering vs Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink). Key asks: preserve client source IP at our app layer, implications for TLS inspection/SNI, minimal firewall ports, and any pricing delta for data egress. Timeline is tight. cc @sam

sam: Quick checklist to decide: 1) Single VPC per region on their side? 2) Exact CIDR ranges we should allow? 3) Will they perform TLS inspection (MITM) or passthrough? 4) Expected throughput (GB/day) and RPS? Note: PrivateLink often terminates the connection at the interface endpoint which can SNAT; preserving src IP usually easier with peering + NLB.

diego: TL;DR: If they need true client src IP in the app, recommend VPC Peering/TGW + NLB (preserves src). PrivateLink (interface endpoints) will give you isolation but client IP is not preserved unless you run an additional header-propagation layer. Also note cross-account PrivateLink requires endpoint service + endpoint acceptance.

anya: Security checklist: PrivateLink keeps traffic off the public internet; good for compliance. If customer does TLS inspection, they'll break end-to-end TLS unless they re-issue certs (or use a passthrough setup). SNI filtering also can be impacted by TLS MITM. We'll need to answer the security questionnaire: traffic flow diagram, cert handling, and whether keys leave customer boundary.

olivia: They responded: ~400GB/day and ~50 steady RPS. They'll likely do TLS inspection at corporate egress in some regions. They want minimal open ports and a pricing estimate.

sam: Pricing notes: PrivateLink = per-hour endpoint charges + data processing/GB + cross-AZ charges. VPC Peering = no endpoint hourly cost but standard cross-account data transfer (depends on cloud provider). For a rough POC estimate: (400 GB/day * 30 days) -> ~12 TB/mo. I can run numbers if they confirm region and expected sustained vs spiky behavior. I can also request a 30-day interface-hour waiver from sales ops for the POC.

diego: Firewall/SG guidance for customer handoff (example, replace placeholders):

```
# Customer inbound SG / Firewall example
Allow inbound: TCP 443 from CUSTOMER_CIDR_1 (e.g., 10.11.0.0/16)
Allow inbound: TCP 80 from OUR_HEALTHCHECK_IPS (35.200.12.34)
Allow outbound: TCP 443 to OUR_EGRESS_IPS (34.120.45.67,34.120.45.68)
# If using NLB in front of instances, source IP will be preserved.
```

And a minimal route example for peering/TGW:

```
# Route table (spoke)
10.1.0.0/16 -> tgw-attach-abc123
0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-01234567 (for customer-managed egress)
# Ensure route propagation on TGW and proper attachment options (transit vs. spoke).
```

olivia: Helpful. Can you also list the exact egress IPs/CIDRs we should tell their network team to allow so they can get a firewall exception?

diego: For POC use these placeholder EIPs — we'll assign concrete EIPs on provisioning but give these now so they can do preflight: 34.120.45.67, 34.120.45.68. Ports: 443 (required), 80 (health), optional: 3478 (STUN) if they plan to do WebRTC through the stack. If they want to lock outbound to only our EIPs, we can provide final list at deploy time.

sam: Preflight test steps to include in handoff:
1) Customer opens SG rules for their spoke: allow inbound TCP 443 from their app subnets to our NLB/endpoint.
2) We provide a curl test: `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.test:443:34.120.45.67 https://api.redwood.test/health` to confirm TLS handshake and cert CN.
3) Run a quick perf test (wrk or vegeta) to validate 50 RPS baseline and catch connection issues.
4) If TLS inspection present, ask them to run the curl test from behind their inspector and share the TLS cert chain.

anya: Add to questionnaire responses: whether keys/certs are customer-managed (if yes, Private Deployment only), whether any packet inspection appliances will terminate TLS (affects SNI), and data residency requirements.

infra-bot: notice: New POC runbook created: https://redwood.internal/docs/poc-privatedeploy-handbook — permissions set for sales, se, eng. Also created ephemeral egress EIP placeholders (will be reconciled at provisioning).

olivia: Great — I'll send the summarized handoff to the customer. @sam can you confirm the interface-hour waiver and a preliminary cost calc for 12 TB/mo? I'll ask the customer for final CIDRs and whether TLS inspection is mandatory.

sam: On it. I'll loop in sales-ops and post numbers by EOD.

diego: I'll draft the formal SG + route table snippet and paste into the handoff doc with exact placeholders to avoid confusion. :thumbsup:
